global_rules: CAPS subject, grade, term and theme are the authority.
Decide whether the assessment needs source material, stimulus material, or no external source before writing questions.
When evidence/stimulus is required, build it before questions.
Every evidence-dependent question must cite a source label, figure label, data table, map, diagram or scenario supplied in the evidence set.
Do not use instruction pages, contents pages, question menus or mark-allocation snippets as source material.
If the material is constructed rather than extracted from an official source, label it as constructed classroom evidence.
Do not fabricate exact official quotations. Use paraphrased extracts, adapted classroom accounts, data, maps, diagrams or visual briefs unless the exact source text is supplied.
Each evidence card must expose usable evidence: dates, actors, places, values, labels, features, claims, perspectives, variables, language features or scenario facts that questions can assess.
Evidence sets must be review-ready but still require educator approval before classroom use.
